name: vscode-lunit-companion
description: Discover and run @rbxts/lunit tests from VS Code's Test Explorer.
author: ShaderCloud

commands.title: Lunit: Show Generated Roblox Studio Bootstrap Script
Lunit: Install Roblox Studio Live-Sync Plugin
Lunit: Show Roblox Studio Live-Sync Status
Lunit: Show Command-Line Test Command (for agents / terminals)

lunit.testGlob.description: Glob pattern (relative to the workspace folder) used to discover Lunit test source files.

lunit.excludeGlob.description: Glob pattern of files/folders to exclude from test discovery.

lunit.explorer.humanizeNames.description: Show camelCase test and class names as readable sentences in the Test Explorer (e.g. "clampsUpToMinWhenTextIsUnderRange" becomes "Clamps up to min when text is under range").

enumDescriptions: The method/class name is the row's label and @DisplayName("...") is shown dimmed beside it as a description (falling back to the first paragraph of the JSDoc comment). Lets you keep method names short and put the full sentence in @DisplayName.
@DisplayName("...") replaces the row's label, matching how Lunit's own console report names the test. The JSDoc comment, if any, becomes the description.
lunit.explorer.displayName.description: How a test's or class's @DisplayName is shown in the Test Explorer tree.

lunit.skipCompile.description: Skip running the compile command before executing tests (use if you compile separately, e.g. with a watch task).

lunit.compileCommand.description: Command used to compile the roblox-ts project to Luau before running tests. Run from the workspace folder root.

lunit.outDir.description: Output directory that rbxtsc compiles Luau into. Used to build ${outDir} in other settings.

lunit.env.description: Additional environment variables to set when running the compile/test commands.

lunit.lune.projectFile.description: Rojo project file describing the DataModel for a roblox-ts game project (--type game), whose compiled output resolves every import through absolute DataModel paths rather than relative ones. Leave empty to detect the project type from the compiled output and pick the Rojo project automatically; set it when several Rojo projects at the workspace root could describe your tests. Ignored for package projects, which keep using lunit.testsRoot / lunit.lunitRoot.

lunit.lune.slowTags.markdownDescription: Tags marking slow tests (matched case-insensitively, on the class or the method), e.g. `["Slow"]`. **Run with Lune** and **Run in Roblox Studio** leave these tests out, and the run report says how many, unless you run a single slow test directly. Setting any tag adds a **Run with Lune (Full)** profile that runs them too (`--full` on the command line).

lunit.lune.parallel.enabled.markdownDescription: Run Lune tests in a pool of independent Lune processes. Each test module is one block, run in its own process with its own module cache; a class-level `@Tag("Parallel")` splits a module further into one block per test method and per `@Each` row, each in a fresh VM and class instance. Workers share no caches or mutable state, so a test that relies on another *module* having run first must be listed with it in `lunit.lune.parallel.dependencyGroups`. Turn this off to run every module in one Lune process, sharing one module cache, as before version 0.7.0.

lunit.lune.parallel.workers.markdownDescription: Maximum number of Lune processes running at once. `0` picks the smaller of 32 and the logical CPU count; the count is always capped by the number of blocks. `1` runs the blocks one after another, still isolated. Larger values such as `64` are allowed: concurrent VM start-ups and memory contend, so whether 64 beats 32 on a 64-core machine depends on the suite (measurements went both ways); measure before raising it. The command line accepts `--workers N` for one run.

lunit.lune.parallel.dependencyGroups.markdownDescription: Test modules that depend on each other, as arrays of module names in prerequisite-first order, e.g. `[["setup.test", "consumer.test"]]`. The modules of a group load into one Lune process and their classes run in that order; a group takes precedence over `@Tag("Parallel")` case splitting. Name a module as the run output shows it (`out/tests/setup.test` for a package project, `ReplicatedStorage.Tests.setup.test` for a game project); a unique trailing part such as `setup.test` or `Tests/setup.test.ts` is enough. Selecting a test in a group also runs the modules listed before its module, in full, and the run output says so. Unknown, ambiguous or repeated names stop the run with an error. A module can belong to one group only.

lunit.lune.executable.description: Command used to invoke Lune (e.g. "lune", "npx lune", or an absolute path), used to run the generated test runner script.

lunit.testsRoot.description: Directory the Lune profile walks recursively for compiled *.test.luau / *.spec.luau files (skipping node_modules). Defaults to the whole workspace folder rather than just ${outDir}, so nested packages with their own tsconfig.json/outDir (e.g. a package embedded in a larger dev workspace, compiled independently of the top-level project) are still found -- no project-specific test folder layout needs configuring. A test file that fails to load under Lune (e.g. a Studio-only test importing something Lune can't run) is skipped with a warning, not a hard failure. Narrow this only if you want the Lune profile to ignore a whole subtree entirely.

lunit.lunitRoot.description: Directory containing the compiled @rbxts/lunit framework, passed to Lune's rbxRequire. Published @rbxts packages normally ship pre-built Luau directly in node_modules rather than being recompiled by rbxtsc, so this is usually node_modules/@rbxts/lunit/out -- override if your project vendors or rebuilds Lunit elsewhere.

lunit.studio.enabled.description: Register a second 'Run in Roblox Studio' test profile (selectable from the Test Explorer run dropdown) alongside the Lune profile.

lunit.studio.executablePath.description: Absolute path to RobloxStudioBeta.exe. Leave blank to auto-detect the latest installed version under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\Versions (Windows).

lunit.studio.rojoProject.description: Rojo project file (relative to the workspace folder, or absolute) that the standalone "Run in Roblox Studio" run builds its temporary place from when no live-synced Studio is connected. A roblox-ts game project (rbxtsc --type game) compiles its tests for one specific Rojo tree, so the place has to come from that same project file. Leave empty to use the *.project.json named by the compile command's --rojo flag (following npm scripts), else default.project.json, else what the compiled output implies. Only a real roblox-ts package (package.json main/types under the output directory, or script-relative compiled output) still gets the extension's own self-contained test project.

lunit.studio.buildPlaceCommand.description: Command that builds the standalone .rbxl place file Studio's CLI opens. ${projectFile} is the Rojo project chosen for the run: your project's own (see lunit.studio.rojoProject) for a roblox-ts game project, or the extension's self-contained, auto-generated test project for a package.

lunit.studio.projectFile.description: Path to the auto-generated, self-contained Rojo project file used to build the test place for a roblox-ts package project. Fully auto-generated and regenerated before every run -- not meant to be hand-edited. Lives in this extension's per-workspace storage, outside your project, by default. A game project builds from its own Rojo project instead (lunit.studio.rojoProject).

lunit.studio.placeFile.description: Path to the local place file built by lunit.studio.buildPlaceCommand and opened by Roblox Studio's --localPlaceFile flag. Lives in this extension's per-workspace storage, outside your project, by default.

lunit.studio.bootstrapScript.description: Luau script passed to Roblox Studio's --runScriptFile flag. Fully auto-generated and regenerated before every run -- not meant to be hand-edited. Lives in this extension's per-workspace storage, outside your project, by default.

lunit.studio.outputFile.description: File Roblox Studio writes script output to (--outputFile), which is parsed for pass/fail results. Lives in this extension's per-workspace storage, outside your project, by default.

lunit.studio.quitAfterExecution.description: Pass --quitAfterExecution so Studio closes automatically once the bootstrap script finishes.

lunit.studio.timeoutSeconds.description: Kill the Studio process if it has not exited after this many seconds (safeguard in case Studio does not quit on its own).

lunit.studio.liveSync.enabled.description: When a Roblox Studio instance is already open with this project live-synced via Rojo, and the companion Lunit Studio plugin (see 'Lunit: Install Roblox Studio Live-Sync Plugin') is installed and polling, run tests there directly instead of building a place and launching a new Studio process -- faster, and doesn't require Play mode. Falls back to the normal build+launch path automatically when no plugin is connected.

lunit.studio.liveSync.port.description: First port in the 20-port localhost discovery range. Each VS Code window takes a free port; select the target workspace using Lunit in Studio. Use the same range in your workspaces. After changing this, reload VS Code and reinstall and reload the Studio plugin.

lunit.studio.liveSync.timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the connected Studio plugin to run the tests and report back before giving up.

lunit.studio.liveSync.syncDelaySeconds.description: After compiling, how long to wait before running tests in the live-synced Studio instance, to give your running `rojo serve` a moment to push the freshly compiled changes in. Increase if results seem to lag one run behind your latest edits.
